title: Pricing-aware region & tier arbitrator: per-customer budget enforcement and GPU-class selection
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: implement a runtime component (the 'Arbitrator') that makes per-request routing decisions across region, tier (on-demand vs spot/preemptible vs reserved), and GPU family (A100/H100/L4/T4) using price and budget constraints. The Arbitrator should enforce hard per-customer monthly spend caps, soft per-route daily budgets, and provide predictable fallback behavior to cheaper model variants when the preferred route would violate budget or capacity SLOs.

Rationale: Customers need predictable inference spend and deterministic degradation paths when we hit budget or capacity limits. Existing cost-aware routing focuses on fleet-level heuristics; this work surfaces per-customer constraints and explicit GPU family preferences into the routing decision graph.

Non-goals: full marketplace-style bidding, dynamic spot bidding, or changing cloud provider selection logic (we will schedule within configured regions). This is about policy enforcement and deterministic fallback mapping integrated with the runtime's smart routing layer.
acceptance_criteria: Arbitrator service deployed behind feature flag and enabled for internal canaries
Per-customer monthly hard spend cap prevents any routed request that would exceed cap; metric 'budget_blocked_requests' exists
Soft daily budgets produce throttles and routing to cheaper tiers with configurable grace thresholds
GPU family preference respected unless blocked by budget or capacity; mapping table editable via Console and API
Fallbacks to lower-cost model variants (quantized / distilled) with preserved schema and SDK compatibility
Integration tests (unit + e2e) demonstrating behavior under simulated price spikes and spot revocations
Dashboard tiles for spend burn rate, blocked-by-budget, and cost delta per-route available in Redwood Console
design_decisions: Enforce budgets at routing time using conservative cost estimates (tokens * model_cost_per_token + fixed infra multiplier) to avoid retroactive overcharge
Two-tier budget model: hard caps (monthly) block requests; soft budgets (daily/route) trigger routing to cheaper variants or rate limit depending on policy
Use GPU family classes (H100, A100, L4) with cost coefficients instead of raw SKU prices to keep decision logic provider-agnostic
Implement policy engine as a sidecar to existing router so we can roll back quickly; expose policy as JSON blobs stored in ConfigDB
Fallback mapping stored per-model: primary -> [variant_low_cost, variant_quantized, variant-distilled] with priorities
Emit decision trace (short tokenized trace) on every routed request for offline audit and replay
implementation_notes: Add new API: POST /v1/policies/{customer_id}/budget to set hard and soft caps
Extend router proto to accept 'budget_estimate' field and return 'arbitration_reason' in response headers
Cost estimator microbenchmarks attached in PR #3367 (uses historical per-token spend for last 7 days, LRU fallback to model catalog price)
Policy enforcement will consult a local cache; cache TTL 15s with optimistic reservations to avoid race conditions under high concurrency
On budget block, return 402-like structured error with reason codes: BUDGET_HARD_BLOCK, BUDGET_SOFT_ROUTED, BUDGET_RATE_LIMITED
Security: policy write endpoints require RBAC scope 'policy.write' and audit log entries are emitted to KMS-protected storage

tests: Unit: cost estimator edge cases (zero tokens, unknown model)
E2E: scenario where daily soft budget crosses threshold -> requests rerouted to quantized variant with preserved response shape
Load: 10k rps canary with budget cache TTL stress and optimistic reservation collisions
Chaos: spot GPU revocation simulation to ensure immediate fallback to on-demand or alternate region within 300ms median additional latency
Billing: simulate per-customer monthly cap crossing to verify blocking and metrics emitted
rollout_plan: 1) Feature-flagged deploy of Arbitrator sidecar to runtime-staging (week 1)
2) Enable for internal customers and test harness (week 2) - monitor 'budget_blocked_requests' and latency impact
3) Canary to 5% of traffic on production with read-only policy evaluation (observer mode) to validate decision trace accuracy (week 3)
4) Enable enforcement for 1-2 low-risk customers with sales-approved budgets (week 4)
5) Gradual enablement to broader customer base and UI release (week 5-6)
Rollback criteria: >5% request error increase, >50ms P95 added latency, or incorrect budget estimate leading to customer-visible overcharge in test accounts
monitoring_and_alerting: Alert: paging for >100 hard blocks/min for a single customer or >0.5% of total traffic
Dashboards: spend burn-rate per-customer, comparator for predicted vs actual spend, per-model variant utilization
Logs: sample decision trace for every 1000 requests stored in trace store for 30 days

notes: Trade-offs discussed: conservative cost estimates reduce overcharge risk but may over-route to cheaper variants; we will tune coefficients with historical reconciliation job
Future work: support per-model SLA classes so critical customers can opt out of soft-routing and instead pay for guaranteed on-demand capacity
Compatibility: client SDKs should surface budget-block error codes and provide helper to retry with 'allow_lower_variant=true' flag
